ideas.title: Icom IC-7300MK2 vs Yaesu FTX-1 vs Xiegu G7250: Which HF Rig in Fall 2026
ideas.why_now: HF radio discussion is up sharply this month, and three of the most talked-about rigs of the year are now in hams' hands. Plenty of people are deciding what to buy before winter operating season.
ideas.angle: A side-by-side buyer's take from hosts who have run all three. It covers who each rig suits (home station, portable, remote), what we liked and what bugged us, and one recommendation per type of operator. This is new because our earlier coverage reviewed each radio on its own and the pending G7250 pitch is a first-contacts video, not a comparison. Fits the OPEN 2026-10-22 YouTube slot.

ideas.title: FreeDV RADE vs SSB: Digital Voice in Half the Bandwidth, Tested On Air
ideas.why_now: RADE is the biggest HF voice story right now. A national league write-up asked whether it will be the next SSB, FlexRadio integration is shipping, and RADE v2 is in testing.
ideas.angle: A hands-on podcast episode. It explains what a machine-learning vocoder is in plain language, shows how RADE fits voice into about 1.5 kHz, and includes recorded on-air comparisons of RADE and SSB on the same path so listeners can hear the difference. It closes with how an everyday ham with a laptop and a rig gets on RADE this winter. Record 2026-11-03 for the OPEN 2026-11-05 podcast slot.

ideas.title: WSJT-X 3.2 Adds JTTY: First Contacts With the New Mode
ideas.why_now: JTTY just arrived in WSJT-X 3.2 and is a trending term in community discussion this week. Early adopters are figuring out settings in public right now.
ideas.angle: Setup through first QSO. It covers what JTTY is (RTTY-like and not locked to UTC time slots like FT8), radio and software settings, and what it feels like compared with FT8 and classic RTTY. It also includes a quick test on a QRP rig, since QMX owners are already asking about it. Edited video for the OPEN 2026-10-29 YouTube slot, plus a Short of the first decode.

ideas.title: Building a Solar MeshCore Repeater for Our Club: Parts, Placement, and Range
ideas.why_now: Off-grid mesh messaging is surging, and competitors are putting out episode after episode on MeshCore repeaters. Michigan clubs are asking whether it is worth adding to their toolkit.
ideas.angle: An everyday-ham build of a ready-to-deploy solar node set up as a MeshCore repeater. It covers what you buy, how to configure it, where to mount it, and a drive test around the area to see real coverage. It frames mesh as a club and ARES companion to ham radio, not a replacement. Fits the OPEN 2026-11-12 YouTube slot.

ideas.title: Working SO-50 With a Handheld: Our First FM Satellite Contacts
ideas.why_now: Satellite listening is having a moment. Another channel's 'anyone can listen' video broke out, and hams are posting SO-50 and RS-44 passes every week. Fall evenings make good pass-chasing weather.
ideas.angle: Take an HT people already own, add a handheld Yagi, and try to make contacts on an FM bird. It covers pass prediction apps, Doppler tuning in plain terms, and the honest misses along with the wins. This is different from the pending SSTV pitches because it is about two-way voice contacts, not receiving images. Fits the OPEN 2026-11-19 YouTube slot.

ideas.title: Retevis and Radioddity Just Filed New Radios With the FCC
ideas.why_now: Four new budget-maker filings landed in the last 45 days, and budget radio discussion is rising. Filings often show up before an announcement.
ideas.angle: A quick Short that explains what an FCC ID filing is, shows the new Retevis and Radioddity entries, and says clearly that a filing is not a product yet. It ends by asking viewers what they hope these turn out to be. Shorts are not tied to the release plan, so this can post any week.

ideas.title: NEXT.POTA.APP Walkthrough With Mike W8MSC: What Changed and Why
ideas.why_now: The new POTA site has been adding features steadily based on user feedback. After a year of debate about where POTA is headed, it helps to show the organization listening.
ideas.angle: A short, practical screen-and-camera walkthrough with Mike W8MSC: the new features, what came from activator feedback, and three things to try on your next activation. Framed as a software walkthrough, not a park trip. This is a deliberate exception because park videos have underperformed here, but the software framing and the host's direct access justify one try. Fits the OPEN 2026-11-26 YouTube slot (a holiday week, which suits a lighter-lift video).

ideas.title: Your ESP32 Has a Hidden SDR Inside
ideas.why_now: The most discussed item in the community this week is several projects independently finding SDR capabilities hiding in cheap ESP32 chips, the same chip family inside some newer ham gadgets.
ideas.angle: A 45-second explainer: what was found, why it matters for cheap homebrew receivers and direction finding, and a pointer to the write-up. It can post as a standalone Short any week and doubles as a podcast news segment for the 2026-11-05 episode.
